properties.name: A Decision can state what it binds, and an unstated scope is visible rather than inferred
properties.statement:
A Decision can declare its SCOPE — node ids, a node type, a region, or free text — and where nobody stated one, the absence is explicit and readable rather than left to inference.

THE GAP THIS CLOSES. A Decision records WHAT was decided and WHY. It does not record WHAT IT APPLIES TO. Six weeks later the question is never "what did we decide" — it is "does that decision cover THIS?", and the node cannot answer.

THE VALUABLE HALF IS THE HONEST ABSENCE, not the field. "Nobody recorded a scope" is a different fact from "scope is everything" and from "scope is this one component", and today all three look identical. An unstated scope must be VISIBLE, not inferred — which is the same shape as the tri-state reflow2 already accepted for rule enforcement (dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking: a rule's power is stated, never defaulted) and as dec:certainty-derived's refusal to let a default assert what nobody chose.

EVIDENCE. A 2-of-3 ruling changed a trigger. Two documents were corrected; a third was found still teaching the old rule — and whether that third file was in scope had two defensible readings. The work stopped there, correctly. The stall was caused by a missing field, not by a hard question.

GENERALITY: this is not a multi-agent problem. A solo developer six months later faces the identical question about their own past decision, with no colleague to ask.

SOURCE: storyflow fleet governance report, api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1. Bound as stated by its author: one project, one month, one fleet shape — hypotheses to test, not requirements.
